title.value: Population Genomics Approaches for Genetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Lineages
title.justification: The paper clearly outlines its focus on utilizing population genomics approaches to characterize genetic lineages of SARS-CoV-2.
title.quote: Population Genomics Approaches for Genetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Lineages

extractions.description: The paper discusses the use of population genomics methods to analyze the genetic diversity and evolution of the SARS-CoV-2 virus during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. It introduces a computational framework leveraging haplotype networks and principal component analysis to monitor the virus's genetic changes and trace infection pathways, supporting real-time lineage identification.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily focused on genetic surveillance and analysis of SARS-CoV-2, which is more related to virology and infectious disease management rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We present here a set of genomic surveillance tools from population genetics which can be used to better understand the evolution of this virus in humans.

primary_category.justification: The focus of the paper does not align with any of the predefined Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories. It is dedicated to genomic analysis of a virus.
primary_category.quote: This computational framework can help design efficient preventive strategies, identify potentially expanding, divergent lineages and derive a fast response against viral adaptation to future therapeutic strategies.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development themes are present since the paper is solely dedicated to SARS-CoV-2 genomic analysis.
secondary_categories.quote: This approach enables real-time lineage identification, a clear description of the relationship between variants of concern, and efficient detection of recurrent mutations.
